songs.title: Stop Trippin'
songs.verdict: A Boston lifer who has been rapping since 2001 links with turntable veterans Solid Vs. Green for a single that sounds, by every account, like it was dug out of a crate on purpose.
songs.body:
M-Dot is Michael Januario, a rapper from Revere, just outside Boston, who has been active since 2001. He played college basketball before going all in on rap, got early exposure opening for Krumb Snatcha on tour in Switzerland, and has built a long independent catalog: a string of mid-2000s mixtapes, the 2017 debut album EgO anD The EneMy, Dining In Dystopia (2022), and a busy run since then, including Shine/Shine On with Method Man in 2025. His collaborator list reads like a boom-bap who's who, from Marley Marl, Pete Rock and Large Professor to Conway The Machine and Elzhi.

"Stop Trippin'" landed in mid-November 2026, produced and cut up by Solid Vs. Green, the veteran duo of DJ Grazzhoppa and Smimooz. It's the first look at a coming joint project, Solid Vs. Green present M-Dot – The Flips, put out through Hip-Hop Enterprise, and there's a four-pack on Bandcamp with the clean, dirty, acapella and instrumental versions for the DJs.

This is squarely in the raw-lyricism, scratched-hook lane M-Dot has worked for two decades, made for people who still care where the cuts come from.
songs.scout_note: Veteran indie boom-bap, not a buzzing newcomer, but well within the underground lane and fresh (theundergroundhiphop.com post dated Nov 18, 2026). Sources: https://theundergroundhiphop.com/m-dot-drops-raw-new-single-stop-trippin-prod-by-solid-vs-green/ (single, producers, label, upcoming The Flips, Bandcamp 4-pack); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-Dot (bio, discography, collaborators). Spotify URL comes from the track embed on the article; I couldn't open Spotify directly to check the listener count (probably low five figures, but check). The artist_url is his Bandcamp from a search result, not the release page. No IG found on an official source.

songs.title: Stay Gold
songs.verdict: A New Haven writer who has been rhyming since age seven brings chipmunk-soul nostalgia and dense wordplay to the title track of his new EP.
songs.body:
Showrocka (Showrocka Pullen) is a New Haven, Connecticut MC who says he has been writing raps since he was seven. In a 2024 interview he counted five solo albums and six collaborative ones since 2019, and he named teaching lyricism at Pendulum Ink with battle-rap figure Chilla Jones and touring the East Coast and the UK. Earlier records include I Grew Up on Wu, with Young Dirty Bastard, and a 2024 single, "Resign," featuring Vallejo's LaRussell. He's also a Recording Academy member.

"Stay Gold" is the title track of an EP that arrived in mid-November 2026. buffaBLOG, which calls him a regular boom-bap presence on the site, points to a chipmunk-soul sample under the beat and to how many references he packs into each line. Singer Indigo Phoenyx handles the hook. No producer is credited in the coverage.

This is classic sample-flip East Coast rap from a Connecticut scene that rarely gets national coverage, made for people who rewind a verse to catch the references.
songs.scout_note: Small, independent New Haven veteran. The 2024 interview said his then-latest single had about 11k listens, so he's well under the threshold. Freshness: buffaBLOG post dated Nov 16, 2026, which calls the EP freshly released. EP album link from the same post: https://open.spotify.com/album/52a3CqY7zDo0Ugy7xPXovc. Sources: https://buffablog.com/showrocka-stay-gold/ (EP, hook singer, sample, track embed, IG link); https://boldjourney.com/?p=655647 (Dec 2024 interview: rapping since seven, discography count, Pendulum Ink, Chilla Jones, LaRussell, touring, Recording Academy); https://www.thewordisbond.com/?p=219067 (2022: I Grew Up on Wu with Young Dirty Bastard). The producer isn't named, so check the credits.

songs.title: isometropia
songs.verdict: A Brighton-raised, London-based rapper raised on drum and bass and The Streets puts his voice over cinematic, understated beats and oklou-ish synth arpeggios.
songs.body:
Rian Brazil is a British rapper from Brighton who now lives in East London. He started rapping at 11 or 12 and later came through the DIY rap trio Nokia Mansion, paying the bills along the way by selling weed and then working as a mortgage rep, before relaunching as a solo artist under the Rian Brazil name. An i-D profile describes a childhood soundtracked by his mum's happy hardcore and his stepdad's drum and bass DJing. It names drum and bass, metal and alt-rap as influences, Mike Skinner most of all, and mentions a Streets sample ("Has It Come to This?"). His solo debut was the four-track EP People like u.

"isometropia" is one half of a new double single that The FADER picked for its Songs You Need In Your Life column on November 18, 2026. The column describes rapping over cinematic, subtle beats and synth arpeggios that recall oklou.

He fits the UK alt-rap lane where the music leans on mood more than drill or grime, and the Mike Skinner influence is his own claim, not a critic's comparison.
songs.scout_note: UK lane pick. Fresh: FADER roundup dated Nov 18, 2026 calls it part of a new double single (I couldn't pin the exact release day or the other track's title). The YouTube URL comes from the FADER embed; YouTube was rate-limited and blocked for me, so I couldn't confirm the video title or channel. Spotify/Apple links not found. The listener count is unknown but looks small (no Viberate stats). Sources: https://www.thefader.com/2026/11/18/songs-you-need-in-your-life-november-18-2026 ; https://i-d.co/?p=416497 (undated profile: Brighton, East London, Nokia Mansion, jobs, influences, People like u EP); https://www.viberate.com/artist/rian-brazil (UK, hip hop). No official IG found.

songs.title: CCTV
songs.verdict: A bitbird and NCS Arcade alum steps out on her own with a five-track hyperpop EP that leans on 140-tempo drums, future-bass sheen and a declared break from playing it safe.
songs.body:
JB Hain is an England-based producer and vocalist who has been putting out music since at least 2021, when blog Heard It Here First profiled her as a 17-year-old blending indie-tinged alternative with trap and future bass. Her early catalog ran through the online future-bass label world: DRIPPING IN ROSES was her home base, she debuted on bitbird via the create together vol.2 compilation alongside Rivus, and her track lose hope (it's all in my head) on found/red passed 100,000 Spotify plays back then. She later landed a release on NCS Arcade too.

CCTV is her first independent release in a while, a five-track EP (TRIPLE 3, limbo, 18/02/2026, mona lisa and something's in the air) that We Rave You covered as out now on 16 November 2026. The outlet frames it as a new era built around perspective and identity, and as a kind of rebirth: more confidence, firmer boundaries. Hain's own line to them was that she is tired of holding on to boundaries, which is a fun contradiction to sit with on a record about drawing new ones.

Sonically, the coverage tags it as hyperpop crossed with 140 and future bass, with an emphasis on storytelling and detailed sound design. Given her roots in the bitbird and NCS orbit, that reads as a lean toward the hyperpop lane from the future-bass side, rather than the other way round.
songs.scout_note: Fresh independent hyperpop/future-bass EP; covered by We Rave You 16 Nov 2026 as 'out now' (exact street date not stated, assume ~mid-Nov 2026). Listener count unknown but she came up through small label compilations (bitbird comp, DRIPPING IN ROSES, NCS Arcade, found/red); a 2021 track 'passing 100k plays' suggests a small audience, so likely well under 100k monthly, but check. Spotify album link taken from the embed on the We Rave You page (embed/album/0m65rSAyKShIfKZlLIlo0o converted). No official IG found. Sources: https://weraveyou.com/2026/11/jb-hain-cctv-ep (EP facts, tracklist, labels history, quote, genre tags); https://hearditherefirst.blog/2021/10/01/jb-hain-lives-in-the-present-moment-with-pulsating-new-single-via-dripping-in-roses/ (England-based, age 17 in 2021, DRIPPING IN ROSES, bitbird comp, lose hope 100k plays). Note: Hain's quote is paraphrased in body. Pronoun 'she' per We Rave You.

songs.title: Hole In My Heart
songs.verdict: Manchester newcomers on Heist or Hit bring a trumpet into jangly, Molina-and-Lenderman-indebted guitar rock on a second single that, per Best Fit, starts sparse and spoken-sung and builds to a loud, chaotic finish.
songs.body:
Wyatt are a Manchester four-piece: brothers Harvey O'Toole (guitar, vocals) and Evan O'Toole (bass, vocals), Emily Mason on trumpet and guitar, and Joe Ward on drums. The brothers grew up playing in their dad's covers band before starting their own. They've come up through Manchester's DIY scene and the artist-led No Band Is An Island collective, supporting TTSSFU, Greg Freeman and Westside Cowboy. They signed to tastemaker label Heist or Hit, which put out their debut single "Morning" in late September. Best Fit described that single as jangle mixed with slacker rock.

"Hole In My Heart" arrived in mid-November along with the announcement of their debut EP A Shout In The Road, due February 19. The EP was made at Airtight studio with Alex Greaves (Yard Act, Gurriers) and Seadna McPhail. The band calls the song a love song that doesn't come down for or against love; it's about trying to make sense of its ups and downs. Harvey first wrote it in his bedroom, and the band built it up in rehearsal after Emily joined. It has since become their set closer.

The band have named MJ Lenderman, Jason Molina, Wilco and The War on Drugs as touchstones, which puts them in the UK's growing alt-country/indie-rock lane. A first headline show at The Abbey in Manchester is set for December 11.
songs.scout_note: Very early-career: the debut single came out on Sep 29 2026, and an earlier interview said they weren't on Spotify yet. Almost certainly well under 100k listeners. They're buzzing in UK indie press (Best Fit Five Day Forecast booking, Clash Next Wave, a Dork interview). The YouTube link was converted from the embed in Clash's article about this single; I couldn't fetch YouTube to confirm the title, so give it a quick check. No Spotify/Bandcamp release link was verified. Sources: https://www.clashmusic.com/?p=465923 (Nov 17 2026: single, EP date, producers, song meaning); https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/tracks/wyatt-hole-in-my-heart (Nov 17 2026: lineup, writing story, set closer, sound); https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/manchester-quartet-wyatt-release-debut-single-morning-on-heist-or-hit (Morning, Heist or Hit, TTSSFU/Greg Freeman tours); https://www.clashmusic.com/next-wave/next-wave-1213-wyatt/ (dad's covers band, No Band Is An Island, Westside Cowboy, Abbey headline); https://www.indieisnotagenre.com/americana-workhorses-wyatt-on-family-manchester-and-the-power-of-bandcamp/ (Lenderman/Molina/Wilco/War on Drugs influences).

songs.title: Last song i sing
songs.verdict: A masked, mostly anonymous Darlington songwriter who moves between fractured alt-pop, bedroom DIY and Frank Ocean-adjacent R&B returns with what Clash calls an introspective, abstract track about finding beauty in the dark.
songs.body:
Pollyfromthedirt is a mostly anonymous, masked songwriter from Darlington in north-east England. The name nods to the town's nickname, The Dirt, and to his mum. He came through with the debut single "There's No Such Thing As England", which Far Out praised for its social commentary. Two EPs followed, The Dirt pt.1 (2025) and The Dirt pt.2, with songs like "Darlo cowboys" and "Blow my lid". Clash made him a Next Wave pick in April 2026, describing a mix of folk balladry and lo-fi.

"Last song i sing" landed in November; Dork and Clash both covered it the week of November 18. Clash says his sound now runs from fractured alt-pop to bedroom DIY to Frank Ocean-adjacent R&B, and describes the new track as introspective and abstract, finding beauty in darkness and raging against the dying of the light. It follows a pair of sold-out London shows, and a London headline at Club Cheek is set for February 10.

He sits in the UK bedroom-pop/alt-pop crossover lane, with festival bookings at Latitude, Dot To Dot and The Great Escape on his record. In his Far Out quick-fire, he joked that Oasis is his biggest musical enemy and said he's into the new Blood Orange album.
songs.scout_note: Spotify track URL converted from the Clash embed (the embed metadata names the track 'Last song i sing' by Pollyfromthedirt). The Clash headline styles the title 'Last one I sing', so I went with the embed/Dork title. The embed metadata hints at a Nov 2 2026 distribution date; press coverage is Nov 18-19. Check the listener count: he has sold-out London shows and festival listings (Latitude, Great Escape, Dot To Dot), so he may be mid-sized. Sources disagree on his base: Clash says he moved to London, Far Out says Manchester. I left that out of the body. Sources: https://www.clashmusic.com/?p=466106 (Nov 19 2026: single, sound, shows); https://www.clashmusic.com/?p=450078 (Apr 2026 Next Wave: name origin, debut single, EPs, songs); https://faroutmagazine.co.uk/quick-fire-questions-10-minutes-with-pollyfromthedirt/ (Dirt pt.1 2025, Oasis/Blood Orange); festival listings from search results (latitudefestival.com, greatescapefestival.com, dottodotfestival.co.uk). The Dork news page was blocked from fetching.

songs.title: Mess
songs.verdict: Nashville's Maddie Kerr, who plays loud enough to call it wall-of-sound, shares a crushing, dramatically sung indie-grunge single about standing by someone at their lowest, ahead of an Alex Farrar-produced debut album.
songs.body:
mercury is the project of Nashville's Maddie Kerr. Her first singles, "Trying" and "Woolgathering", came out in late 2023. Next came the EP and short film Together We Are One, You And I, the Swarm The Hive Mind EP in late 2024, and the singles "Faster", "Justin's Headed Out" and "Heaven". Stereogum, Paste, Kerrang! and Guitar World have covered her. In 2026 she played Pickathon and spent the fall supporting holywatr across North America.

"Mess" came out November 18 on Big Loud Rock with a video by Eliot Lee. It's the second preview of her debut album, The Real Thing, The Determiner, after September's "Roar Of The Heliac Goat". Alex Farrar, whose credits include Wednesday and MJ Lenderman, produced the album over several stormy days at his Drop Of Sun studio in Asheville. Best Fit says the song is about what it means to support someone through their darkest moments. The album as a whole traces a darkness Kerr has carried since her early twenties, through broken friendships and first relationships in a small town, to the point where she forgives herself.

Stereogum calls the album grungy, heartland-tinged shoegaze with melodramatic flair. That puts her near the Farrar-adjacent Asheville/Nashville guitar scene. Treefort and Best Kept Secret are on her 2027 calendar.
songs.scout_note: CHECK LISTENER COUNT: she's the most-covered act in this batch (Stereogum, Kerrang!, Rolling Stone mentions, North American support tour) and may be near or over 100k monthly listeners. Big Loud Rock is an independent label, not a major. YouTube URL converted from the embed in Stereogum's 'Mess' article; I couldn't fetch YouTube directly. No Spotify link verified. Album date conflict: Best Fit says Feb 19 2027, Stereogum says 2/27, so the body leaves the date out. Sources: https://stereogum.com/2518559/mercury-announces-debut-album-the-real-thing-the-determiner-hear-mess/music (Nov 18 2026: label, video, producer, sound, tour dates); https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/mercury-reveals-plans-for-debut-album-the-real-thing-the-determiner (song meaning, album themes, Drop Of Sun, Farrar credits); https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Mercury-to-Tour-North-America-Fall-2026-With-New-Single-20260930 (discography history, press, Pickathon, holywatr tour). The 'wall-of-sound' wording in the verdict comes from a search-result headline (inkl/Guitar World interview); I didn't fetch that page.

songs.title: Toy (ft. Ukweli & tg.blk)
songs.verdict: A Nairobi songwriter with Teyana Taylor credits opens her new Kenyan-collab EP with a breezy under-two-minute neo-soul cut that hands the mic to a Mombasa rapper midway.
songs.body:
Xenia Manasseh was born and raised in Nairobi, studied music business at Berklee, then spent years as a signed songwriter in Atlanta before heading home. Her Swahili-and-English single "Niambie" (2019) broke her in Kenya, followed by the EPs Fallin' Apart and Maybe (the latter made with producer Ukweli) and the 2023 debut album LOVE / HATE Pt. 1. Behind the scenes she has written and sung backgrounds for Teyana Taylor, which put her name on a Best R&B Album Grammy nomination for Escape Room, and she sang backup on Berhana's Tiny Desk.

"Toy" is the opening track of NBO 'X' PRESS, an eight-song EP that landed on November 12, 2026 on Soul Headquarters. It is a short one, under two minutes, built with Nairobi producer and visual artist Ukweli and featuring tg.blk, a self-taught rapper-singer-producer from Mombasa. The wider EP pulls in a whole Kenyan cast: Maali, Blinky Bill, Wuod Baba and Ywaya Tajiri, with Kobby Worldwide and Hendrick Sam also among the producers.

Stereofox filed it under neo-soul and R&B, pointing to her warm vocal, a relaxed rap verse and a crisp beat with a cool bassline. It reads as a deliberately local, crew-first project after the more globe-trotting debut album.
songs.scout_note: Fresh Kenyan alt-R&B; EP NBO 'X' PRESS out Nov 12, 2026 (Qobuz) / covered Nov 13 by KenyanVibe; Stereofox posted 'Toy' Nov 20. Spotify link from Stereofox player. Underground check: no major label (Soul Headquarters per Qobuz; earlier Cinq Music distribution), but she has Apple Music Africa 'Ones To Watch' 2023, Spotify EQUAL/RADAR, COLORS and a writer Grammy nom, so CHECK monthly listeners, may sit near or above 100k. Qobuz credits 'Toy' main artist as Ukweli feat. tg.blk under Xenia's EP, so credit may display differently. No official IG verified. Sources: https://www.stereofox.com/xenia-manasseh-toy-ft-ukweli-tg-blk/ ; https://www.qobuz.com/fr-fr/album/nbo-x-press-xenia-manasseh/c8ftphythwqcy ; https://www.kenyanvibe.com/crispy-fresh-new-kenyan-music-this-week-19/ ; https://thenativemag.com/for-the-girls-xenia-manasseh/ ; https://www.kbc.co.ke/?p=118600 ; https://www.citizen.digital/entertainment/kenyan-rb-star-xenia-manasseh-featured-on-american-live-music-show-tiny-desk-n337077

songs.title: When It Rains In August
songs.verdict: An Amsterdam-raised, LA-based singer who learned to sing by studying Daniel Caesar and SZA turns an old heartbreak into a seven-track EP that wanders between soul, pop and a rock-leaning detour.
songs.body:
Jaïr Faria was born in Amsterdam, went to arts school there, started in a dance academy, picked up piano and guitar, and was writing songs by about 14. His father is a known Dutch singer-songwriter. He has said he taught himself to sing by studying Daniel Caesar, H.E.R. and SZA, and that TikTok covers were what first reached US listeners. After a first EP made with Amsterdam producers he moved to Los Angeles, where he now writes with producers and songwriters through Roc Nation. Singles "Georgia" and "August" came earlier in 2026.

When It Rains In August is a seven-track EP that EARMILK covered as newly out on November 6, 2026. Faria told them it draws on a breakup from a few years back: missing someone, second-guessing, trying to move on and getting stuck in between. "August" is where the project started, and "Cry About It" was first written for another artist before he reworked it in a rockier direction. Ratings Game Music singled out "We'll Be Okay" as a focus track for its stripped-back production.

EARMILK tags him across alt R&B, neo-soul, pop and alt-rock, so this sits on the soft, confessional edge of the lane rather than the club end.
songs.scout_note: Spotify album link converted from the EARMILK embed of the EP. Exact release date not stated anywhere I could read; EARMILK called it newly released on Nov 6, 2026 and Ratings Game reviewed a focus track Nov 12, so likely late Oct/early Nov, please confirm. UNDERGROUND DOUBT: EARMILK says he works 'through Roc Nation' (could be publishing/dev deal, not clear it's a label deal); listener count unknown, check. Leans pop as much as R&B. IG handle from EARMILK's artist links. Sources: https://earmilk.com/2026/11/06/jair-faria-new-ep-when-it-rains-in-august-interview/ ; https://ratingsgamemusic.com/2026/11/12/jair-faria-well-be-okay-song-review/ ; https://artistrack.com/jair-faria-august-single/

songs.title: Baby 3.0
songs.verdict: A hip-hop-rooted London selector with a bootleg habit (Angie Stone, Jeremih) delivers three distorted-bassline electro and tech cuts on Rosie Ama's Human Endeavour imprint.
songs.body:
GoodMostlyBad is the DJ and producer alias of Mehar Bedi, playing mostly in London with RA-listed bookings stretching to Amsterdam, Paris, Helsinki, Bern and Bangkok. Beatportal put her in its emerging-artists list this month, noting her production started out in hip-hop, rap and R&B before she moved into techno, electro and odd experimental club tracks. Her Bandcamp is stacked with earlier EPs (Shawty 3.0 on Scuffed Recordings, Pum Pum City, SPLAT!) and cheeky edits of Jeremih's "Birthday Sex" and Angie Stone; past labels also include Reel Long Overdub, Bad Tips and Earful of Wax.

Baby 3.0 came out November 20, 2026 on Human Endeavour (HE015), the Ransom Note sub-label run by Rosie Ama. It is three tracks: "Home Gurl" (the lead), "Cam Gurl" and "Baby Gurl", mixed by Roshan Chauhan and mastered by Justin Drake. The Bandcamp notes frame it as a sequel to Shawty 3.0: four-on-the-floor drums, busy percussion and distorted basslines under warped synths, but brighter than before, about coming out the other side of a rough patch.

Boomkat files it under electro; her own tags run from leftfield electro to tech house and 'wiggly'. It's a pick for the club end of the queue.
songs.scout_note: Very underground: Spotify artist page shows ~194 monthly listeners. Release date and credits confirmed on her Bandcamp release page and Boomkat (HE015, 20 Nov 2026). No release-specific Spotify/SoundCloud/YouTube link found; soundcloud_url is her ARTIST page (listed on both RA and her Bandcamp), bandcamp_url is the exact EP. Location conflict: RA/Beatportal say London-based, her Bandcamp location tag says India; body says London-based play. Lane is more electro/tech than jersey club or UKG. songs.title: No Problem (feat. Bryte)
songs.verdict: The Rinse FM host and 'Arthi Hard' party-starter puts an MC up front on a track from her debut EP, built for the garage-to-funky swing her DJ sets are known for.
songs.body:
Arthi Nachiappan is a Chennai-born, London-based DJ, dancer and sometime journalist who runs the We're Gonna Arthi Hard party, where Katy B, Donae'o and Roska have shown up. She holds a show on Rinse FM mixing dancehall, reggaeton, afrobeats, UK garage and funky, and before DJing took over she danced in videos for Beyoncé, Charli XCX, Dave and Kali Uchis. Her productions have been slowly arriving: "RUFFEST" with Sam Interface on FABRICLIVE's Carnival EP in 2025, then "Maayam" with Pritt in May 2026.

"No Problem" featuring Bryte is the second track on Chromatic, her debut EP, out November 20, 2026 via FABRICLIVE. The EP also has Dismantle and £MONZO on "Ijoya", Sam Interface on "Madrugada", plus BLVK H3RO and BRAVA, and it closes with a vocal mix of this one. Her Bandcamp notes say the EP moves through the moods of her club sound and was sparked by the DJ sets that got her producing in the first place.

Beatportal, naming her an emerging artist this month, lists garage, soca, funky house, kuduro and bassline in the mix.
songs.scout_note: Fresh: Chromatic EP dated Nov 20, 2026 on her Bandcamp (FABRICLIVE). SoundCloud track URL comes from a search-result listing titled 'Stream No Problem (feat. Bryte) by Arthi Nachiappan' (SoundCloud blocks fetching, so please click-check). Could also review the full EP instead (bandcamp_url). UNDERGROUND CHECK: not a major-label artist, but a fairly established DJ (Parklife, Lost Village, Sonar/DGTL bookings, Beyoncé dancer); production catalogue is small, so streaming numbers are probably modest, check. Lane: UKG/funky/bassline club. No official IG confirmed (aggregator lists arthi.nachiappan). Bryte not researched.
